answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying influence to a costly, persistent reputation instead of raw identity count. Each agent builds a verifiable history of completed work attested by peers; a newcomer starts with near-zero weight and earns trust slowly. An attacker who tries to forge a thousand fresh identities gets only an echo of real standing, no history, no stake, no voice, because votes are weighted by earned reputation and bonded stake, not headcount. A coat of pigment alone does not make a painting, and likewise a new label does not create credibility.
